name: fs-operation-scope-enforced
body: Law (prose; assessed by review): a filesystem operation (`apg_rm` / `apg_mv` / `apg_cp`) may touch ONLY a path granted by the acting agent's EFFECTIVE `edit`-action rules in its opencode 2.x `permissions` array — the source path, and for mv/cp the destination path as well. The TOOL enforces this: it evaluates the acting agent's effective `edit` rules — the ordered combination of the lower-priority configuration, the global rules, and the agent's own entries, with the LAST matching entry winning — resolves the rule set and the candidate path in ONE consistent frame, and refuses a path outside that scope; the tool applies its OWN fail-closed default and refuses a path matched by zero entries, where opencode itself resolves a zero-match to `ask`; enforcement does not live in opencode's matching of the tool's path argument. The fs scope tracks the effective `edit` scope, so a `deny` the `edit` action honours also refuses the fs operation. The boundary is the PROJECT WORKTREE: for a code-writer, a path that resolves into the main checkout (outside every project worktree) is refused regardless of the caller-supplied directory, and no operation may cross the project/worktree boundary. The capability is never granted as a blanket `"*": allow`: the grant is deny-by-default with the role's owned globs allowed under `apg/.worktrees/*/` only. The tools perform plain filesystem operations only — they are not `git rm`/`git mv` — and they never mutate graph nodes (that is `apg node rm` / `apg edge rm`).
